newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to raise wheat import tax to 15 pct from 3.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to raise wheat import tax to 15 pct from 3.

text.p: Turkey has prepared a decree to raise customs tax on wheat imports by private companies to 15 percent from the present three percent after a higher domestic wheat crop in 1996/97, a senior farm official said on Wednesday.
"The decree is ready and may come out any time," said the official.
"The increase will cover all kinds of wheat including durum and milling wheat. It will be added on the C and F price," he said.
He said the move aimed to limit or "virtually stop" wheat imports by private millers and pasta producers which he said had imported about 800,000 tonnes of various kinds of wheat so far this year.
The Turkish Grain Board (TMO), the government agency which buys grain from farmers, is exempt from the customs tax.
The official said the TMO had bought about 650,000 tonnes of wheat -- including 450,000 tonnes of durum and the rest milling wheat -- and 650,000 tonnes of barley from farmers so far this year.
The TMO will hold a tender on Thursday to export at least 200,000 tonnes of barley.

Officials said the TMO could export some durum wheat later in the year if local pasta producers, which imported 200,000 tonnes of durum from June 1995 to May 1996, did not want to buy local durum, which producers say has some quality problems.

Agricultural ministry officials said earlier Turkey was expecting 19 million tonnes of wheat output this year, up from 15.5 million in 1995/96, but reports by Western traders said the 1996/97 harvest could not exceed 16.5 million tonnes.
